concepts.title: 1. The Sridharacharya / Quadratic Formula
concepts.subtitle: Find roots directly from a, b, and c
concepts.summary: For ax²+bx+c=0 with a≠0, use x=(-b±√(b²−4ac))/(2a).
concepts.trap: Forgetting −b or the factor 2 in the denominator.

concepts.title: 2. Discriminant
concepts.subtitle: Calculate the expression under the radical
concepts.summary: The discriminant D=b²−4ac is calculated before evaluating the quadratic formula.
concepts.trap: Changing the subtraction sign or coefficient signs.

concepts.title: 3. Substitution and Root Simplification
concepts.subtitle: Evaluate both formula branches
concepts.summary: Insert a, b, and D, simplify √D, and evaluate the plus and minus branches separately.

concepts.title: 4. Variable Substitution
concepts.subtitle: Reduce transformable higher-order equations
concepts.summary: Use y=x² when an equation in x⁴ and x² can become a quadratic in y, then solve it with the quadratic formula and back-substitute.

points.text: Solve the reduced quadratic with the formula.

concepts.title: 5. Exact Radical and Fraction Handling
concepts.subtitle: Preserve algebraic precision
concepts.summary: Keep radicals and fractions exact during quadratic-formula calculations.
concepts.trap: Rounding too early or changing signs.

schema_notes.topic_scope: This file is exclusively for the Quadratic Formula topic. It does not contain another solving-method question type. Transformable equations are included only when the reduced equation is solved using the quadratic formula.
schema_notes.atomic_progression: Direct, large-coefficient, and radical questions use identify coefficients → calculate D → substitute → simplify both roots. Transformable questions use substitution → reduced coefficients → D → back-substitution.
schema_notes.strict_option_rule: Every strategy option contains both an algebraic instruction and an actual mathematical result, expression, equation, or value.
schema_notes.latex_compliance: All equations, worked examples, and rubric mathematics use multiline aligned LaTeX with at most one equals sign per line.
schema_notes.guided_calculation_compliance: Every step has exactly two vertically stacked outputs; every field uses placeholder Enter value; prompts and labels do not reveal answers.
schema_notes.pool_compliance: Each typology contains exactly 12 unique questions: 4 Easy, 4 Medium, 4 Hard.
